claim: Zebrafish Gdf3 (Dvr1) is a member of the TGFβ superfamily of cell signaling ligands that includes Xenopus Vg1 and mammalian Gdf1/3.
source: Zebrafish Gdf3 (Dvr1) is a member of the TGFβ superfamily of cell signaling ligands that includes Xenopus Vg1 and mammalian Gdf1/3.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the classification and relationships of Gdf3 within the TGFβ superfamily.

claim: Engineered homozygous mutants of zebrafish gdf3 have no apparent phenotype.
source: Surprisingly, engineered homozygous mutants in zebrafish have no apparent phenotype.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental generation and analysis of gdf3 mutants.

claim: Elimination of Gdf3 in oocytes of maternal-zygotic mutants results in embryonic lethality.
source: Elimination of Gdf3 in oocytes of maternal-zygotic mutants results in embryonic lethality that can be fully rescued with gdf3 RNA, demonstrating that Gdf3 is required only early in development, beyond which mutants are viable and fertile.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of maternal-zygotic mutant phenotypes.

claim: Maternal-zygotic gdf3 mutant embryonic lethality can be fully rescued with gdf3 RNA.
source: Elimination of Gdf3 in oocytes of maternal-zygotic mutants results in embryonic lethality that can be fully rescued with gdf3 RNA, demonstrating that Gdf3 is required only early in development, beyond which mutants are viable and fertile.
evidence: This is demonstrated through RNA injection rescue experiments.

claim: Gdf3 is required only early in development, beyond which mutants are viable and fertile.
source: Elimination of Gdf3 in oocytes of maternal-zygotic mutants results in embryonic lethality that can be fully rescued with gdf3 RNA, demonstrating that Gdf3 is required only early in development, beyond which mutants are viable and fertile.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing that early RNA injection allows mutants to develop normally.

claim: Gdf3 mutants are refractory to Nodal ligands.
source: Gdf3 mutants are refractory to Nodal ligands and Nodal repressor Lefty1.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of Nodal ligand effects in gdf3 mutants.

claim: Gdf3 mutants are refractory to Nodal repressor Lefty1.
source: Gdf3 mutants are refractory to Nodal ligands and Nodal repressor Lefty1.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of Lefty1 effects in gdf3 mutants.

claim: Signaling driven by TGFβ ligand Activin remains intact in gdf3 mutants.
source: Signaling driven by TGFβ ligand Activin and constitutively active receptors Alk4 and Alk2 remain intact in gdf3 mutants, indicating that Gdf3 functions at the same pathway step as Nodal.
evidence: This is demonstrated through Activin signaling experiments in gdf3 mutants.

claim: Signaling driven by constitutively active receptor Alk4 remains intact in gdf3 mutants.
source: Signaling driven by TGFβ ligand Activin and constitutively active receptors Alk4 and Alk2 remain intact in gdf3 mutants, indicating that Gdf3 functions at the same pathway step as Nodal.
evidence: This is demonstrated through CA-Alk4 signaling experiments in gdf3 mutants.

claim: Signaling driven by constitutively active receptor Alk2 remains intact in gdf3 mutants.
source: Signaling driven by TGFβ ligand Activin and constitutively active receptors Alk4 and Alk2 remain intact in gdf3 mutants, indicating that Gdf3 functions at the same pathway step as Nodal.
evidence: This is demonstrated through CA-Alk2 signaling experiments in gdf3 mutants.

claim: Gdf3 functions at the same pathway step as Nodal.
source: Signaling driven by TGFβ ligand Activin and constitutively active receptors Alk4 and Alk2 remain intact in gdf3 mutants, indicating that Gdf3 functions at the same pathway step as Nodal.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that downstream signaling is intact while Nodal signaling is not.

claim: Exogenous gdf3 is able to fully rescue mutants only when co-expressed with endogenous Nodal.
source: Targeting gdf3 and ndr2 RNA to specific lineages indicates that exogenous gdf3 is able to fully rescue mutants only when co-expressed with endogenous Nodal.
evidence: This is demonstrated through lineage-specific targeting experiments.

claim: Gdf3 is an essential cofactor of Nodal signaling during establishment of the embryonic axis.
source: Together, these findings demonstrate that Gdf3 is an essential cofactor of Nodal signaling during establishment of the embryonic axis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the experimental findings.

claim: vg1 was the first-known regionally localized RNA in a vertebrate oocyte, localized to the vegetal pole of the egg.
source: vg1, another member of the TGFβ family, was prototypically described as the first-known regionally localized RNA in a vertebrate oocyte, localized to the vegetal pole of the egg, and subsequently in early embryos (Rebagliati et al., 1985).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rebagliati et al., 1985.

claim: Humans and other mammals have two vg1 orthologues, GDF1 and GDF3.
source: Humans and other mammals have two vg1 orthologues, GDF1 and GDF3, and zebrafish have a single orthologue, gdf3, previously known as dvr1.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the evolutionary relationships of vg1 orthologues.

claim: Zebrafish have a single vg1 orthologue, gdf3, previously known as dvr1.
source: Humans and other mammals have two vg1 orthologues, GDF1 and GDF3, and zebrafish have a single orthologue, gdf3, previously known as dvr1.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about zebrafish gdf3.

claim: Maternal Vg1 is required for early zygotic expression of anterior mesendodermal genes in Xenopus.
source: Studies in Xenopus have suggested that maternal Vg1 is required for early zygotic expression of anterior mesendodermal genes (Birsoy et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Birsoy et al., 2006.

claim: Overexpression of Xenopus Vg1 fusion proteins in specific early cell lineages can fully invert the LR axis.
source: Vg1 has been implicated in early Left-Right patterning, as overexpression of Xenopus Vg1 fusion proteins or mouse Gdf1 fusion proteins in specific early cell lineages can fully invert the LR axis (Hyatt et al., 1996; Hyatt and Yost, 1998; Wall et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hyatt et al., 1996; Hyatt and Yost, 1998; Wall et al., 2000.

claim: Overexpression of mouse Gdf1 fusion proteins in specific early cell lineages can fully invert the LR axis.
source: Vg1 has been implicated in early Left-Right patterning, as overexpression of Xenopus Vg1 fusion proteins or mouse Gdf1 fusion proteins in specific early cell lineages can fully invert the LR axis (Hyatt et al., 1996; Hyatt and Yost, 1998; Wall et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hyatt et al., 1996; Hyatt and Yost, 1998; Wall et al., 2000.

claim: Vg1 is the only known member of the TGFβ family with early LR patterning capability.
source: Vg1 is the only known member of the TGFβ family with this early LR patterning capability.
evidence: This is stated as a distinguishing characteristic of Vg1 based on existing knowledge.

claim: Overexpression or grafts of Xenopus Nodal (Xnr1) in right lateral plate can invert asymmetry at later stages of development.
source: At later stages of development, overexpression or grafts into lateral plate mesoderm that activate TGFβ family member Xenopus Nodal (Xnr1) in right lateral plate can also invert asymmetry (Ohi and Wright, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ohi and Wright, 2007.

claim: In mice, homozygous knockout mutations of Gdf1 have altered asymmetry.
source: In mice, homozygous knockout mutations have altered asymmetry (Rankin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rankin et al., 2000.

claim: Genetic variants in human GDF1 have been implicated in complex congenital heart defects.
source: In humans, genetic variants in GDF1 have been implicated in complex congenital heart defects (Karkera et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2015), likely to be effects of upstream altered LR patterning.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Karkera et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2015.

claim: Human GDF1 congenital heart defects are likely effects of upstream altered LR patterning.
source: In humans, genetic variants in GDF1 have been implicated in complex congenital heart defects (Karkera et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2015), likely to be effects of upstream altered LR patterning.
evidence: This is inferred from the known role of GDF1 in LR patterning.

claim: gdf3 RNA and protein are abundantly stored in the zebrafish oocyte and early embryo before zygotic gene activation.
source: Similar to vg1 in Xenopus, gdf3 RNA and protein are abundantly stored in the oocyte and early embryo before zygotic gene activation in zebrafish (Helde and Grunwald, 1993; Peterson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Helde and Grunwald, 1993; Peterson et al., 2013.

claim: Kupffer's vesicle is the ciliated organ of asymmetry in zebrafish.
source: In zebrafish, Kupffer's vesicle (KV), the ciliated organ of asymmetry (Essner et al., 2005; Essner et al., 2002), contains motile cilia that generate asymmetric fluid flow and LR patterning information that is transmitted to lateral plate mesoderm (LPM), which then conveys LR patterning information to the brain, heart and gut primordia (Dasgupta and Amack, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Essner et al., 2005; Essner et al., 2002.

claim: Kupffer's vesicle contains motile cilia that generate asymmetric fluid flow and LR patterning information.
source: In zebrafish, Kupffer's vesicle (KV), the ciliated organ of asymmetry (Essner et al., 2005; Essner et al., 2002), contains motile cilia that generate asymmetric fluid flow and LR patterning information that is transmitted to lateral plate mesoderm (LPM), which then conveys LR patterning information to the brain, heart and gut primordia (Dasgupta and Amack, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dasgupta and Amack, 2016.

claim: LR patterning information from Kupffer's vesicle is transmitted to lateral plate mesoderm.
source: In zebrafish, Kupffer's vesicle (KV), the ciliated organ of asymmetry (Essner et al., 2005; Essner et al., 2002), contains motile cilia that generate asymmetric fluid flow and LR patterning information that is transmitted to lateral plate mesoderm (LPM), which then conveys LR patterning information to the brain, heart and gut primordia (Dasgupta and Amack, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dasgupta and Amack, 2016.

claim: Lateral plate mesoderm conveys LR patterning information to the brain, heart and gut primordia.
source: In zebrafish, Kupffer's vesicle (KV), the ciliated organ of asymmetry (Essner et al., 2005; Essner et al., 2002), contains motile cilia that generate asymmetric fluid flow and LR patterning information that is transmitted to lateral plate mesoderm (LPM), which then conveys LR patterning information to the brain, heart and gut primordia (Dasgupta and Amack, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dasgupta and Amack, 2016.

claim: Zebrafish gdf3 is expressed in tissues implicated in LR patterning including cells adjacent to the KV, in the LPM and in heart primordia.
source: Zebrafish gdf3 is expressed in tissues implicated in LR patterning including cells adjacent to the KV, in the LPM and in heart primordia.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about gdf3 expression patterns.

claim: Morpholino knockdown of gdf3 results in normal KV structure, KV cilia length and motility, and normal asymmetric KV fluid flow.
source: Morpholino knockdown of gdf3 results in normal KV structure, KV cilia length and motility, and normal asymmetric KV fluid flow, but disruption of downstream LR patterning in the LPM.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Peterson et al., 2013 in the preceding sentence.

claim: Morpholino knockdown of gdf3 results in disruption of downstream LR patterning in the LPM.
source: Morpholino knockdown of gdf3 results in normal KV structure, KV cilia length and motility, and normal asymmetric KV fluid flow, but disruption of downstream LR patterning in the LPM.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Peterson et al., 2013 in the preceding sentence.

claim: Zebrafish Gdf3 was proposed to transmit LR information generated by KV cilia flow to LPM.
source: Thus, zebrafish Gdf3 was proposed to transmit LR information generated by KV cilia flow to LPM (Peterson et al., 2013), and the reasonable expectation was that mutants of gdf3 in zebrafish would have LR patterning defects.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Peterson et al., 2013.

claim: The reasonable expectation was that mutants of gdf3 in zebrafish would have LR patterning defects.
source: Thus, zebrafish Gdf3 was proposed to transmit LR information generated by KV cilia flow to LPM (Peterson et al., 2013), and the reasonable expectation was that mutants of gdf3 in zebrafish would have LR patterning defects.
evidence: This is inferred from the proposed function of Gdf3 in LR patterning.

claim: Homozygous zygotic gdf3 mutants develop normally and do not show alterations in LR patterning.
source: Surprisingly, homozygous zygotic mutants develop normally and do not show alterations in LR patterning.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of zygotic mutant phenotypes.

claim: Zebrafish mutants in which the maternal stores of Gdf3 are eliminated have an embryonic lethal phenotype.
source: On the other hand, zebrafish mutants in which the maternal stores of Gdf3 are eliminated have a much more dramatic embryonic lethal phenotype, which we analyzed for a wide range of tissue specification and embryonic patterning pathways.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of maternal-zygotic mutant phenotypes.

claim: Gdf3 functions as an obligate co-factor of Nodal.
source: Results from a series of epistasis experiments and cell-lineage targeted rescues of gdf3 mutants indicate that Gdf3 functions as an obligate co-factor of Nodal, and that Nodal functions as an obligate cofactor of Gdf3.
evidence: This is inferred from epistasis and lineage-targeting experiments.

claim: Nodal functions as an obligate cofactor of Gdf3.
source: Results from a series of epistasis experiments and cell-lineage targeted rescues of gdf3 mutants indicate that Gdf3 functions as an obligate co-factor of Nodal, and that Nodal functions as an obligate cofactor of Gdf3.
evidence: This is inferred from epistasis and lineage-targeting experiments.

claim: Neither Nodal nor Gdf3 can function without the other in fundamental patterning of the vertebrate embryonic axis.
source: These results indicate that neither Nodal nor Gdf3 can function without the other in fundamental patterning of the vertebrate embryonic axis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: TALENs were designed to target genomic sequences encoding the first few amino acids of the pro-domain of Gdf3.
source: We generated mutant alleles of gdf3 by using TALENs designed to target genomic sequences encoding the first few amino acids of the pro-domain of Gdf3 (Figure 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is described in the methods and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: High resolution melt analysis (HRMA) was used to screen for mutations in genomic DNA from embryos of G0 founders.
source: High resolution melt analysis (HRMA) (Parant et al., 2009) was used to screen for mutations in genomic DNA from embryos of G0 founders and later, from fin clips from adults derived from those founders (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is described in the methods with citation to Parant et al., 2009 and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: gdf3zy51 and gdf3zy52 alleles both result in reading frame shifts which encode missense amino acids and early termination codons.
source: The results presented here utilize gdf3zy51 and gdf3zy52 alleles; both mutations result in reading frame shifts which encode missense amino acids and early termination codons, suggesting they may be functional nulls (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: gdf3zy51 and gdf3zy52 alleles may be functional nulls.
source: The results presented here utilize gdf3zy51 and gdf3zy52 alleles; both mutations result in reading frame shifts which encode missense amino acids and early termination codons, suggesting they may be functional nulls (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from the nature of the mutations (frameshift with early termination).

claim: The phenotypes are indistinguishable between gdf3 mutants carrying either the zy51 or zy52 allele.
source: The phenotypes are indistinguishable between gdf3 mutants carrying either the zy51 or zy52 allele and these mutants are used and described interchangeably.
evidence: This is based on phenotypic observations of both alleles.

claim: gdf3zy53 has a 6 bp in-frame deletion that removes two amino acids but leaves the predicted protein otherwise unchanged.
source: A third mutant line, gdf3zy53, has a 6 bp in-frame deletion that removes two amino acids but leaves the predicted protein otherwise unchanged and had no observable phenotype.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of the gdf3zy53 allele.

claim: gdf3zy53 had no observable phenotype.
source: A third mutant line, gdf3zy53, has a 6 bp in-frame deletion that removes two amino acids but leaves the predicted protein otherwise unchanged and had no observable phenotype.
evidence: This is based on phenotypic observations of the gdf3zy53 allele.

claim: Wild-type and zygotic gdf3 mutants were phenotypically indistinguishable.
source: (D) Wild-type (WT) and (E) zygotic (Z) gdf3 mutants were phenotypically indistinguishable.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D,E comparing WT and Zgdf3 embryos.

claim: Maternal-zygotic gdf3 mutants lacked notochord and pharyngeal endoderm.
source: (F) Maternal-zygotic (MZ) gdf3 mutants lacked notochord, pharyngeal endoderm and had reduced anterior neural tissues.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1F of MZgdf3 embryos.

claim: Maternal-zygotic gdf3 mutants had reduced anterior neural tissues.
source: (F) Maternal-zygotic (MZ) gdf3 mutants lacked notochord, pharyngeal endoderm and had reduced anterior neural tissues.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1F of MZgdf3 embryos.

claim: MZgdf3 mutants were completely rescued by injection of 100 pg gdf3 RNA at the one-cell stage.
source: (G) MZgdf3 mutants were completely rescued by injection of 100 pg gdf3 RNA at the one-cell stage.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1G of rescued MZgdf3 embryos.

claim: ta (ntl) expression in the notochord was absent from MZgdf3 although tailbud expression was maintained.
source: (H, I) ta (ntl) expression in the notochord was absent from MZgdf3 although tailbud expression was maintained.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1H,I comparing ta expression in WT and MZgdf3.

claim: tbx16 (spt) expression in spinal cord neurons was absent in MZgdf3 while tailbud expression is unaffected.
source: (J, K) tbx16 (spt) expression in spinal cord neurons was absent in MZgdf3 while tailbud expression is unaffected.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1J,K comparing tbx16 expression in WT and MZgdf3.

claim: Trunk and tail somites expressing myod1 were reduced in number and altered in shape in MZgdf3.
source: (L, M) Trunk and tail somites expressing myod1 were reduced in number and altered in shape in MZgdf3.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1L,M comparing myod1 expression in WT and MZgdf3.

claim: Expression of hand2 in the heart, pharyngeal arch mesoderm and pectoral fin buds is absent in MZgdf3.
source: (N, O) Expression of hand2 in the heart, pharyngeal arch mesoderm and pectoral fin buds is absent in MZgdf3.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1N,O comparing hand2 expression in WT and MZgdf3.

claim: Ventral neural tissues and pharyngeal endoderm expressing foxa2 (axial) were absent in MZgdf3.
source: (P–S) Ventral neural tissues and pharyngeal endoderm expressing foxa2 (axial) were absent in MZgdf3.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1P-S comparing foxa2 expression in WT and MZgdf3.

claim: Patterns of expression of otx2 in the forebrain and midbrain were altered in MZgdf3 mutants.
source: Patterns of expression of otx2 in the forebrain and midbrain (T, U), and erg2b (krox20) in hindbrain rhobomeres 3 and 5 (V, W) were altered in MZgdf3 mutants.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1T,U comparing otx2 expression in WT and MZgdf3.

claim: Patterns of expression of erg2b (krox20) in hindbrain rhobomeres 3 and 5 were altered in MZgdf3 mutants.
source: Patterns of expression of otx2 in the forebrain and midbrain (T, U), and erg2b (krox20) in hindbrain rhobomeres 3 and 5 (V, W) were altered in MZgdf3 mutants.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1V,W comparing erg2b expression in WT and MZgdf3.

claim: In embryos derived from crosses of gdf3zy51 heterozygous parents 90% had left-sided spaw expression, 2% right-sided, and 8% bilateral expression.
source: In embryos derived from crosses of gdf3zy51 heterozygous parents 90% had left-sided, 2% right-sided, and 8% bilateral expression (five clutches; n = 163 embryos total).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 with quantification of spaw expression patterns.

claim: The distribution of normal left-sided spaw expression in embryos derived from gdf3 heterozygotes was not significantly different to that in embryos derived from wild-type AB strain parents.
source: The distribution of normal left-sided expression in embryos derived from gdf3 heterozygotes was not significantly different to that in embryos derived from wild-type AB strain parents (93% left, 2.5% right, 4.5% bilateral; n = 197, from four clutches; Pearson X2 test – p=0.463).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 with statistical analysis.

claim: Homozygous zygotic gdf3 mutant adults are fertile.
source: Homozygous zygotic gdf3 mutant adults are fertile.
evidence: This is based on observations of breeding homozygous mutants.

claim: In-crosses of homozygous gdf3 mutants yielded Maternal Zygotic (MZgdf3) embryos that exhibit a pronounced phenotype at 24 hpf, with 100% penetrance.
source: In-crosses of homozygous mutants yielded Maternal Zygotic (MZgdf3) embryos that exhibit a pronounced phenotype at 24 hpf, with 100% penetrance (N > 100) (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is based on observations of MZgdf3 embryos shown in Figure 1F.

claim: At 24–26 hpf, MZgdf3 embryos lack a notochord and spinal cord.
source: At 24–26 hpf, MZgdf3 embryos lack a notochord and spinal cord and structures associated with lateral plate mesoderm including the heart, and have greatly reduced anterior neural development reflected in the narrowed neural tube, un-folded brain and reduced tissue between the eyes resulting in cyclopia (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 of MZgdf3 embryos.

claim: At 24–26 hpf, MZgdf3 embryos lack structures associated with lateral plate mesoderm including the heart.
source: At 24–26 hpf, MZgdf3 embryos lack a notochord and spinal cord and structures associated with lateral plate mesoderm including the heart, and have greatly reduced anterior neural development reflected in the narrowed neural tube, un-folded brain and reduced tissue between the eyes resulting in cyclopia (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 of MZgdf3 embryos.

claim: MZgdf3 embryos have greatly reduced anterior neural development reflected in the narrowed neural tube, un-folded brain and reduced tissue between the eyes resulting in cyclopia.
source: At 24–26 hpf, MZgdf3 embryos lack a notochord and spinal cord and structures associated with lateral plate mesoderm including the heart, and have greatly reduced anterior neural development reflected in the narrowed neural tube, un-folded brain and reduced tissue between the eyes resulting in cyclopia (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 of MZgdf3 embryos.

claim: Injection of 100 pg gdf3 mRNA fully rescued over 90% of the MZgdf3 embryos.
source: Injection of 100 pg gdf3 mRNA fully rescued over 90% of the MZgdf3 embryos, and these fully rescued embryos could survive until adulthood and survivors were fertile.
evidence: This is based on rescue experiments with quantification of outcomes.

claim: Fully rescued MZgdf3 embryos could survive until adulthood and survivors were fertile.
source: Injection of 100 pg gdf3 mRNA fully rescued over 90% of the MZgdf3 embryos, and these fully rescued embryos could survive until adulthood and survivors were fertile.
evidence: This is based on observations of rescued embryos raised to adulthood.

claim: Of 22 rescued MZgdf3 embryos selected for an inflated swim bladder at 6 days post-fertilization and raised to adulthood, 14 survived.
source: For example, of 22 rescued MZgdf3 embryos selected for an inflated swim bladder at 6 days post-fertilization and raised to adulthood, 14 survived.
evidence: This is based on tracking of rescued embryos to adulthood.

claim: 5 mating pairs of rescued MZgdf3 adults produced clutches of embryos with the MZgdf3 phenotype at 24 hpf, demonstrating fertility of both males and females.
source: From those, 5 mating pairs produced clutches of embryos with the MZgdf3 phenotype at 24 hpf, demonstrating fertility of both males and females that were derived from Gdf3 null embryos that received only a pulse of WT gdf3 mRNA shortly after fertilization.
evidence: This is based on breeding experiments with rescued adults.

claim: The mutant phenotype of embryos derived from reciprocal crosses was solely dependent on a gdf3−/− maternal genotype; the paternal genome did not alter the phenotype.
source: To assess whether both maternal and paternal contributions to the zygote were necessary for the MZgdf3 phenotype, we performed reciprocal pairwise crosses of male and female MZgdf3 homozygotes to either Zgdf3 heterozygotes or to wild-type fish and found that the mutant phenotype of the derived embryos was solely dependent on a gdf3−/− maternal genotype; the paternal genome did not alter the phenotype.
evidence: This is based on reciprocal cross experiments.

claim: Embryos derived from gdf3−/− males showed no mutant phenotype when derived from a heterozygous female with a wildtype allele of gdf3.
source: Embryos derived from gdf3−/− males showed no mutant phenotype when derived from a heterozygous female with a wildtype allele of gdf3 (n = 4 mating pairs).
evidence: This is based on reciprocal cross experiments.

claim: Paternal contribution of a wild-type gdf3 allele could not rescue embryos derived from MZgdf3 females.
source: Strikingly, paternal contribution of a wild-type gdf3 allele could not rescue embryos derived from MZgdf3- females (n = 7 mating pairs with gdf3+/− male; n = 3 mating pairs with WT +/+ males).
evidence: This is based on reciprocal cross experiments.

claim: gdf3+/− heterozygotes that were derived from gdf3 null eggs and wildtype sperm displayed the MZgdf3 phenotype.
source: In other words, gdf3+/− heterozygotes that were derived from gdf3 null eggs and wildtype sperm displayed the MZgdf3 phenotype.
evidence: This is based on reciprocal cross experiments.

claim: The paternal genome was transcriptionally activated following zygotic gene activation (ZGA) in embryos from a cross of MZgdf3 female by WT male.
source: To assess whether the paternal genome was transcriptionally activated following zygotic gene activation (ZGA) in embryos from a cross of MZgf3 female by WT male cross, we carried out RT-PCR to compare cDNA samples prepared from pre-ZGA 1000 cell-stage and post-ZGA 90% epiboly, and 18 somite-stage embryos, and compared those to samples at the same time points derived from embryos from a MZgdf3 in-cross and a WT cross (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: WT gdf3 transcript was detected in all stages of WT embryos and was absent from cDNA derived from homozygous MZgdf3 embryos.
source: WT gdf3 transcript was detected in all stages of WT embryos (lanes C1-3) and was absent from cDNA derived from homozygous MZgdf3 embryos (serving to indicate that the WT primers do not amplify the maternal or paternal mutant allele; lanes C7-9).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5C RT-PCR analysis.

claim: WT transcript was undetectable in pre-ZGA stage embryos (1000 cell stage) derived from a cross of a MZgdf3 mutant female by WT male, but was present in cDNA derived from post-ZGA stages.
source: WT transcript was also undetectable in pre-ZGA stage embryos (1000 cell stage, lane 4) derived from a cross of a MZgdf3 mutant female by WT male, but was present in cDNA derived from post-ZGA stages (lanes C4, 5).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5C RT-PCR analysis.

claim: Post-ZGA expression of paternal WT gdf3 does not rescue the MZ phenotype.
source: Although the paternal WT genome is clearly activated in MZgdf3 embryos, this post-ZGA expression of paternal WT gdf3 does not rescue the MZ phenotype.
evidence: This is based on the observation that embryos with paternal WT gdf3 still show the MZ phenotype.

claim: In MZgdf3 embryos, the notochord was absent as evidenced by the lack of ta expression in the midline; expression in the tailbud remains.
source: In MZgdf3 embryos, the notochord was absent as evidenced by the lack of ta expression in the midline; expression in the tailbud remains (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1I WISH analysis of ta expression.

claim: Expression of tbx16 (spt) was maintained in the tailbud of MZgdf3 embryos but tbx16 expression in a subset of spinal cord neurons in WT embryos was not detected in MZgdf3 mutants.
source: Expression of another T-box transcription factor tbx16 (spt), expressed in paraxial and ventral mesoderm, was maintained in the tailbud of MZgdf3 embryos but tbx16 expression in a subset of spinal cord neurons in WT embryos was not detected in MZgdf3 mutants (Figure 1J,K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1J,K WISH analysis of tbx16 expression.

claim: The ventral mesoderm marker eve1 was expressed in the tailbud of both WT and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: Similarly, the ventral mesoderm marker eve1 was expressed in the tailbud of both WT and MZgdf3 embryos (not shown).
evidence: This is based on WISH analysis (data not shown).

claim: In MZgdf3 embryos, myod1 expression occurred in fewer, smaller, u-shaped somites restricted to the caudal trunk and tail.
source: In similar stage MZgdf3 embryos, myod1 expression occurred in fewer, smaller, u-shaped somites restricted to the caudal trunk and tail (Figure 1L,M).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1L,M WISH analysis of myod1 expression.

claim: All hand2 expression domains (heart tube, pharyngeal mesoderm, pectoral fin bud) were absent in MZgdf3.
source: In WT embryos hand2 was expressed in the heart tube, a derivative of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm, in the pharyngeal mesoderm of the branchial arches and in the pectoral fin bud. All of these tissue-specific expression domains were absent in MZgdf3 (Figure 1N,O).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1N,O WISH analysis of hand2 expression.

claim: All foxa2 (axial) expression domains were absent in MZgdf3 mutant embryos.
source: The forkhead box transcription factor foxa2 (axial) was expressed in the midline in the ventral brain, the spinal floorplate and the chorda-neural hinge as well as laterally in the pharyngeal endoderm of the branchial arches. All of these expression domains were absent in MZgdf3 mutant embryos (Figure 1P–S).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1P-S WISH analysis of foxa2 expression.

claim: The rostral-most regions of the neural tube were relatively unaffected in MZgdf3 embryos.
source: The rostral-most regions of the neural tube were relatively unaffected in MZgdf3 embryos.
evidence: This is based on analysis of anterior neural markers.

claim: Expression domains of otx2 and egr2b (krox20) were present though somewhat misproportioned and misshapen in MZgdf3 mutant embryos versus WT embryos.
source: Expression domains of otx2 in the forebrain and midbrain, and egr2b (krox20) in hindbrain rhombomeres 3 and 5 were present though somewhat misproportioned and misshapen in MZgdf3 mutant embryos versus WT embryos (Figure 1T–W).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1T-W WISH analysis of otx2 and egr2b expression.

claim: Maternally provided Gdf3 is essential in the patterning of mesoderm, endoderm and in some aspects of neural development.
source: Together, these results indicate that maternally provided Gdf3 is essential in the patterning of mesoderm, endoderm and in some aspects of neural development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression analysis in MZgdf3 mutants.

claim: The MZgdf3 phenotypes are strikingly similar to phenotypes of mutant embryos lacking maternal Nodal signaling components.
source: The MZgdf3 phenotypes described above are strikingly similar to phenotypes of mutant embryos lacking maternal Nodal signaling components such as in double homozygous mutants for ndr1;ndr2 (sqt;cyc), MZtdgf1 (MZoep) and MZfoxh1 (Dougan et al., 2003; Gritsman et al., 1999; Slagle et al., 2011), or from overexpression of the Nodal antagonists lft1 or lft2 (Bisgrove et al., 1999; Thisse and Thisse, 1999).
evidence: This is based on comparison to published phenotypes with citations.

claim: The Nodal family member ndr2 was expressed in anterior and posterior axial mesoderm and anterior axial neurectoderm in WT embryos.
source: The Nodal family member ndr2 was expressed in anterior and posterior axial mesoderm and anterior axial neurectoderm (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A WISH analysis of ndr2 expression.

claim: WT ndr2 expression pattern was unchanged in embryos injected with gdf3 RNA.
source: This WT expression pattern was unchanged in embryos injected with gdf3 RNA (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B WISH analysis.

claim: MZgdf3 embryos were void of any detectable ndr2 expression.
source: In contrast, MZgdf3 embryos were void of any detectable ndr2 expression, but the normal expression pattern could be completely restored by injection of gdf3 RNA (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C WISH analysis.

claim: The normal ndr2 expression pattern could be completely restored in MZgdf3 by injection of gdf3 RNA.
source: In contrast, MZgdf3 embryos were void of any detectable ndr2 expression, but the normal expression pattern could be completely restored by injection of gdf3 RNA (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2D WISH analysis.

claim: The normal expression patterns of lft1 and lft2 were absent in MZgdf3 embryos.
source: The normal expression patterns of lft1 in marginal mesendoderm, the axial chordamesoderm, prechordal plate mesoderm and anterior ventral neurectoderm) and lft2 in posterior axial neurectoderm and prechordal plate mesoderm (Figure 2E,I) were absent in MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 2G,K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2G,K WISH analysis.

claim: Neither lft1 nor lft2 gene expression pattern was altered in WT embryos injected with gdf3 RNA.
source: Neither gene expression pattern was altered in WT embryos injected with gdf3 RNA (Figure 2F,J), and gdf3 RNA injection fully rescued expression of both of these Nodal response genes in MZgdf3 (Figure 2H,L).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2F,J WISH analysis.

claim: gdf3 RNA injection fully rescued expression of lft1 and lft2 in MZgdf3.
source: Neither gene expression pattern was altered in WT embryos injected with gdf3 RNA (Figure 2F,J), and gdf3 RNA injection fully rescued expression of both of these Nodal response genes in MZgdf3 (Figure 2H,L).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2H,L WISH analysis.

claim: lft1 and lft2 expression are absent from MZgdf3 embryos at shield stage during mesendoderm formation.
source: These results, and the observation that lft1 and lft2 expression are absent from MZgdf3 embryos at shield stage during mesendoderm formation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicate that the MZgdf3-deficient phenotype was not due to hyperexpression of endogenous lft1 and lft2.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 WISH analysis.

claim: The MZgdf3-deficient phenotype was not due to hyperexpression of endogenous lft1 and lft2.
source: These results, and the observation that lft1 and lft2 expression are absent from MZgdf3 embryos at shield stage during mesendoderm formation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicate that the MZgdf3-deficient phenotype was not due to hyperexpression of endogenous lft1 and lft2.
evidence: This is inferred from the absence of lft1 and lft2 expression in MZgdf3.

claim: The transcription factors ta and gsc are direct targets of Nodal signaling.
source: The transcription factors ta and gsc are direct targets of Nodal signaling and overlap with the expression of ndr2 in the midline. (Chen and Schier, 2001; Thisse et al., 1994)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen and Schier, 2001; Thisse et al., 1994.

claim: In MZgdf3 embryos midline gsc and ta expression domains were absent while ta expression in the marginal mesendoderm was unaffected.
source: In MZgdf3 embryos midline gsc and ta expression domains were absent while ta expression in the marginal mesendoderm was unaffected (Figure 2O).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2O WISH analysis.

claim: Injection of gdf3 RNA fully rescued the axial expression domains of both ta and gsc in MZgdf3.
source: Injection of gdf3 RNA fully rescued the axial expression domains of both ta and gsc (Figure 2P).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2P WISH analysis.

claim: In MZgdf3 mutant embryos axial tbx16 expression in the prechordal plate was absent and the width of the paraxial expression domain was reduced.
source: In MZgdf3 mutant embryos axial tbx16 expression in the prechordal plate was absent and the width of the paraxial expression domain was reduced (Figure 2S).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2S WISH analysis.

claim: Injection of gdf3 RNA into WT embryos did not alter normal tbx16 domains but was capable of fully rescuing expression in the prechordal plate and expanding the paraxial expression domain to a normal width in MZgdf3.
source: Injection of gdf3 RNA into WT embryos did not alter normal tbx16 domains but was capable of fully rescuing expression in the prechordal plate and expanding the paraxial expression domain to a normal width (Figure 2T).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2T WISH analysis.

claim: In MZgdf3 embryos the width of eve1 expression domain was reduced, but was fully restored to normal width by the injection of gdf3 at the 1–2 cell stage.
source: In MZgdf3 embryos the width of this expression domain was reduced, but was fully restored to normal width by the injection of gdf3 at the 1–2 cell stage (Figure 2W,X).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2W,X WISH analysis.

claim: In MZgdf3, no sox17-expressing cells were detected in the blastoderm and in most embryos (14 of 16) no expression was detected in cells at the dorsal margin.
source: In MZgdf3, no sox17-expressing cells were detected in the blastoderm and in most embryos (14 of 16) no expression was detected in cells at the dorsal margin.
evidence: This is based on WISH analysis with quantification.

claim: sox17 expression in the presumptive endoderm and dorsal forerunner cells of MZgdf3 was restored by injection of gdf3.
source: sox17 expression in the presumptive endoderm and dorsal forerunner cells of MZgdf3 was restored by injection of gdf3 (Figure 2B').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B' WISH analysis.

claim: In MZgdf3 embryos foxa2 expression in the endoderm was absent and in the majority of embryos, expression in the axis was absent.
source: In MZgdf3 embryos foxa2 expression in the endoderm was absent and in the majority of embryos, expression in the axis was absent. In a few embryos (3 of 15) one or two foxa2-expressing cells were present at the dorsal margin (Figure 2E').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2E' WISH analysis with quantification.

claim: foxa2 expression in MZgdf3 embryos was rescued to a normal pattern by injected gdf3 RNA.
source: foxa2 expression in MZgdf3 embryos was rescued to a normal pattern by injected gdf3 RNA (Figure 2F').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2F' WISH analysis.

claim: In MZgdf3 embryos a triangular otx2 expression domain was present but greatly reduced in size, failing to extend to the animal pole.
source: In MZgdf3 embryos a triangular otx2 expression domain was present but greatly reduced in size, failing to extend to the animal pole (Figure 2I').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2I' WISH analysis.

claim: otx2 expression was fully restored to a normal pattern in MZgdf3 embryos by expression of exogenous gdf3 RNA.
source: Like all of the marker genes examined here, otx2 expression was fully restored to a normal pattern in MZgdf3 embryos by expression of exogenous gdf3 RNA (Figure 2J').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2J' WISH analysis.

claim: Nodal signaling response pathways are dependent on Gdf3 function.
source: Together, these results indicate that Nodal signaling response pathways are dependent on Gdf3 function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression analysis.

claim: Injection of ndr1 or ndr2 RNA into MZgdf3 embryos did not rescue gsc or ta expression in the dorsal germ ring of shield stage embryos.
source: In contrast, injection of ndr1 or ndr2 RNA into MZgdf3 embryos did not rescue gsc or ta expression in the dorsal germ ring of shield stage embryos, did not rescue axial tissues in embryos at 24 hpf, and did not induce a dorsalized phenotype (Figure 3P–R,V–X).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3P-R,V-X.

claim: Injection of ndr1 or ndr2 RNA into MZgdf3 embryos did not rescue axial tissues in embryos at 24 hpf.
source: In contrast, injection of ndr1 or ndr2 RNA into MZgdf3 embryos did not rescue gsc or ta expression in the dorsal germ ring of shield stage embryos, did not rescue axial tissues in embryos at 24 hpf, and did not induce a dorsalized phenotype (Figure 3P–R,V–X).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3P-R,V-X.

claim: Injection of ndr1 or ndr2 RNA into MZgdf3 embryos did not induce a dorsalized phenotype.
source: In contrast, injection of ndr1 or ndr2 RNA into MZgdf3 embryos did not rescue gsc or ta expression in the dorsal germ ring of shield stage embryos, did not rescue axial tissues in embryos at 24 hpf, and did not induce a dorsalized phenotype (Figure 3P–R,V–X).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3P-R,V-X.

claim: Nodal signaling ligands cannot activate the nodal signaling pathway in the absence of Gdf3.
source: These results indicate that Nodal signaling ligands cannot activate the nodal signaling pathway in the absence of Gdf3, and gives genetic evidence that Nodal and Gdf3 function at the same step in the signaling pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the inability of Nodal ligands to rescue MZgdf3.

claim: Nodal and Gdf3 function at the same step in the signaling pathway.
source: These results indicate that Nodal signaling ligands cannot activate the nodal signaling pathway in the absence of Gdf3, and gives genetic evidence that Nodal and Gdf3 function at the same step in the signaling pathway.
evidence: This is genetic evidence from epistasis experiments.

claim: Lefty proteins are negative regulators of the Nodal signaling pathway.
source: Lefty proteins are negative regulators of the Nodal signaling pathway (Bisgrove et al., 1999; Thisse and Thisse, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bisgrove et al., 1999; Thisse and Thisse, 1999.

claim: Injection of lft1 RNA into WT embryos resulted in a loss of gsc expression and a reduction in dorsal expression domain of ta.
source: Injection of lft1 RNA into WT embryos resulted in a loss of gsc expression and a reduction in dorsal expression domain of ta (Figure 3Y,Z), and lacked midline tissues including notochord, pharyngeal mesoderm and endoderm and ventral brain at 24 hpf (Figure 3A').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3Y,Z,A'.

claim: Injection of lft1 RNA into MZgdf3 did not exacerbate their defective patterns or phenotypes.
source: Importantly, injection of lft1 RNA into MZgdf3 did not exacerbate their defective patterns or phenotypes (compare Figure 3B', C', D' with Figure 3D,E,F), indicating that there no residual Nodal signaling in MZgdf3 embryos that can be further antagonized by exogenous Lft1.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B',C',D' compared to Figure 3D,E,F.

claim: There is no residual Nodal signaling in MZgdf3 embryos that can be further antagonized by exogenous Lft1.
source: Importantly, injection of lft1 RNA into MZgdf3 did not exacerbate their defective patterns or phenotypes (compare Figure 3B', C', D' with Figure 3D,E,F), indicating that there no residual Nodal signaling in MZgdf3 embryos that can be further antagonized by exogenous Lft1.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect of Lft1 in MZgdf3.

claim: The TGFβ ligand Activin signals through Type I and Type II Activin Receptors; subsets of which are also utilized in the propagation of Nodal signaling.
source: The TGFβ ligand Activin signals through Type I and Type II Activin Receptors; subsets of which are also utilized in the propagation of Nodal signaling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Activin signaling.

claim: Ectopic expression of Activin in both WT and MZgdf3 embryos resulted in massive ectopic expression of gsc and ta at shield stage.
source: Ectopic expression of Activin in both WT and MZgdf3 embryos resulted in massive ectopic expression of gsc and ta at shield stage (Figure 3E',F',G',H',I').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3E'-I'.

claim: Exogenous expression of Activin in MZgdf3 embryos partially rescued the mutant phenotype at 24 hpf.
source: Exogenous expression of Activin in MZgdf3 embryos partially rescued the mutant phenotype at 24 hpf (Figure 3J').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3J'.

claim: Alk4 functions as a Type I receptor for multiple TGF beta-related ligands to regulate dorsal mesoderm induction and left-right axis determination in Xenopus.
source: Alk4 functions as a Type I receptor for multiple TGF beta-related ligands to regulate dorsal mesoderm induction and left-right axis determination in Xenopus (Chen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2004.

claim: Alk2 is important in the BMP signaling pathway.
source: Alk2 is important in the BMP signaling pathway (Branford et al., 2000), and in zebrafish (acvr1l) is implicated in the specification of ventral mesoderm (Mintzer et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Branford et al., 2000.

claim: In zebrafish, Alk2 (acvr1l) is implicated in the specification of ventral mesoderm.
source: Alk2 is important in the BMP signaling pathway (Branford et al., 2000), and in zebrafish (acvr1l) is implicated in the specification of ventral mesoderm (Mintzer et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mintzer et al., 2001.

claim: Injection of CA-Alk4 RNA into either WT or MZgdf3 embryos caused ectopic expression of both gsc and ta at shield stage.
source: Injection of CA-Alk4 RNA into either WT or MZgdf3 embryos caused ectopic expression of both gsc and ta at shield stage (Figure 3K', L', N', O').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3K',L',N',O'.

claim: At 24hpf, CA-Alk4 injected WT embryos were partially dorsalized, and injected MZgdf3 embryos were partially rescued having some notochord present and largely normal anterior morphology.
source: At 24hpf, injected WT embryos were partially dorsalized, and injected MZgdf3 embryos were partially rescued having some notochord present and largely normal anterior morphology (Figure 3M', P').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3M',P'.

claim: At 24 hpf, CA-Alk2 caused a severe ventralization of WT embryos characterized by loss of dorsal structures such as the notochord, expanded and misshapen somites and a reduction in anterior structures including the brain and eyes.
source: At 24 hpf, CA-Alk2 caused a severe ventralization of the embryo characterized by loss of dorsal structures such as the notochord, expanded and misshapen somites and a reduction in anterior structures including the brain and eyes (Figure 3S').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3S'.

claim: The absence of gsc expression in shield stage MZgdf3 was not rescued in embryos injected with CA-Alk2, but ta expression was expanded into the dorsal domain of the margin that normally lacked expression.
source: The absence of gsc expression in shield stage MZgdf3 was not rescued in embryos injected with CA-Alk2, but ta expression was expanded into the dorsal domain of the margin that normally lacked expression, indicating an expansion of more lateral or ventral mesoderm domains (Figure 3T', U').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3T',U'.

claim: MZgdf3 embryos at 24 hpf injected with CA-Alk2 showed a phenotype consistent with ventralization, having further reduced anterior mesoderm and neural structures including the complete loss of eyes.
source: Similar to CA-Alk2 injected WT embryos, MZgdf3 embryos at 24 hpf showed a phenotype consistent with ventralization, having further reduced anterior mesoderm and neural structures including the complete loss of eyes (Figure 3V').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3V'.

claim: The downstream components of the Nodal signaling pathway are intact and capable of activation in MZgdf3 mutants.
source: These results indicate that the downstream components of the Nodal signaling pathway are intact and capable of activation in MZgdf3 mutants, and suggest that Gdf3 acts at the same level in the pathway as Nodal, as an agonist for the activation of Alk4 (Acvr1ba).
evidence: This is inferred from the ability of CA-Alk4 and Activin to activate signaling in MZgdf3.

claim: Gdf3 acts at the same level in the pathway as Nodal, as an agonist for the activation of Alk4 (Acvr1ba).
source: These results indicate that the downstream components of the Nodal signaling pathway are intact and capable of activation in MZgdf3 mutants, and suggest that Gdf3 acts at the same level in the pathway as Nodal, as an agonist for the activation of Alk4 (Acvr1ba).
evidence: This is inferred from the epistasis experiments.

claim: MZgdf3 embryos were only fully rescued when gdf3-expressing targeted cells had contributed to midline tissues including the notochord and prechordal plate mesoderm.
source: Strikingly, MZgdf3 embryos were only fully rescued when gdf3-expressing targeted cells had contributed to midline tissues including the notochord and prechordal plate mesoderm (37 of 131 embryos) (Figure 4D), or in midline and non-midline tissues (62 of 131).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D with quantification.

claim: When targeted cells were confined to non-midline tissues, ectopic gdf3 expression rescued only the posterior structures of MZgdf3 embryos, including posterior notochord, but did not rescue anterior structures such as the ventral brain and eyes.
source: When targeted cells were confined to non-midline tissues (32 of 131), ectopic gdf3 expression rescued only the posterior structures of MZgdf3 embryos, including posterior notochord, but did not rescue anterior structures such as the ventral brain and eyes (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E with quantification.

claim: gsc expression was rescued in MZgdf3 when targeted cells were either in the midline or contiguous and adjacent to the midline.
source: gsc expression was rescued when targeted cells were either in the midline (10 of 74 embryos, Figure 4O) or contiguous and adjacent to the midline (42 of 74, Figure 4P).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4O,P with quantification.

claim: When targeted cells were confined to regions outside the dorsal midline, gsc expression was not rescued by ectopic gdf3 expression in MZgdf3.
source: In contrast, when targeted cells were confined to regions outside the dorsal midline, gsc expression was not rescued by ectopic gdf3 expression (22 of 74, Figure 4Q).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4Q with quantification.

claim: Confinement of ndr2-expressing targeted cells to midline tissues in WT embryos gave a relatively mild phenotype that included a kinked notochord.
source: In WT embryos, confinement of ndr2-expressing targeted cells to midline tissues (34 of 118 embryos) gave a relatively mild phenotype that included a kinked notochord (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4F with quantification.

claim: In WT embryos in which ndr2 targeted cells contributed to non-midline tissues, hyperdorsalization phenotypes with extremely disorganized tissues were observed.
source: This is in striking contrast to hyperdorsalization phenotypes with extremely disorganized tissues in WT embryos in which targeted cells contributed to non-midline tissues (32 of 118) (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1), or from ubiquitous ndr2 expression (Figure 3U).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1 with quantification.

claim: In WT embryos ndr2 induces ectopic expression of gsc in sectors that correspond to the targeted cells, regardless of whether targeted cells are located at the dorsal midline, adjacent to the midline, or at a location distant from the midline.
source: When analyzed at the shield stage, in WT embryos ndr2 induces ectopic expression of gsc in sectors that correspond to the targeted cells, regardless of whether targeted cells are located at the dorsal midline (11 of 64 embryos, Figure 4S), adjacent to the midline (31 of 64, Figure 4T), or at a location distant from the midline (22 of 64, Figure 4U).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4S,T,U with quantification.

claim: Targeted expression of ndr2 in MZgdf3 embryos by injection at the 4–8 cell stage had no effect, that is, could not rescue, irrespective of whether targeted cells localized to prospective midline or non-midline tissues.
source: In contrast to the effects of ndr2 ectopic expression in WT embryos, targeted expression of ndr2 in MZgdf3 embryos by injection at the 4–8 cell stage had no effect, that is, could not rescue, irrespective of whether targeted cells localized to prospective midline or non-midline tissues (n = 53 embryos: 11 midline, 17 non-midline, 25 broad expression) (Figure 4H,I).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4H,I with quantification.

claim: Overexpression of ndr2 in spatially restricted clones of cells in MZgdf3 embryos failed to induce gsc expression, regardless of the location of targeted cells.
source: When analyzed at the shield stage, overexpression of ndr2 in spatially restricted clones of cells in MZgdf3 embryos failed to induce gsc expression, regardless of the location of targeted cells (n = 47, Figure 4W–Y).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4W-Y with quantification.

claim: In the absence of gdf3, regardless of lineage, ndr2 had no apparent function; it could not induce shield-stage expression of gsc and could not rescue the MZgdf3 phenotype.
source: Thus, in the absence of gdf3, regardless of lineage, ndr2 had no apparent function; it could not induce shield-stage expression of gsc and could not rescue the MZgdf3 phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lineage-targeting experiments.

claim: The ability of ectopic gdf3 to fully rescue MZgdf3 embryos only when it is expressed in lineages that co-express Nodal indicates that Gdf3 and Nodal must be co-expressed to have function.
source: The ability of ectopic gdf3 to fully rescue MZgdf3 embryos only when it is expressed in lineages that co-express Nodal, and the observation that MZgdf3 embryos are refractory to Nodal (ndr2) overexpression phenotypes seen in WT embryos, indicate that Gdf3 and Nodal must be co-expressed to have function, and that either ligand alone cannot function without the other.
evidence: This is inferred from the lineage-targeting experiments.

claim: Either Gdf3 or Nodal ligand alone cannot function without the other.
source: The ability of ectopic gdf3 to fully rescue MZgdf3 embryos only when it is expressed in lineages that co-express Nodal, and the observation that MZgdf3 embryos are refractory to Nodal (ndr2) overexpression phenotypes seen in WT embryos, indicate that Gdf3 and Nodal must be co-expressed to have function, and that either ligand alone cannot function without the other.
evidence: This is inferred from the lineage-targeting experiments.

claim: Maternally supplied Gdf3 is required during early embryonic development.
source: Maternally supplied Gdf3 is required during early embryonic development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the MZgdf3 phenotype.

claim: Zygotic gdf3 homozygous mutant embryos have no apparent morphological phenotype, and can grow to viable and fertile adults.
source: Zygotic gdf3 homozygous mutant embryos have no apparent morphological phenotype, and can grow to viable and fertile adults.
evidence: This is based on observations of zygotic mutants.

claim: Embryos generated from fertilization of a gdf3-deficient mutant egg by a wildtype gdf3+ sperm display the same embryonic lethal MZgdf3 mutant phenotype as those fertilized with sperm from a homozygous gdf3- mutant father.
source: In contrast, embryos generated from fertilization of a gdf3-deficient mutant egg by a wildtype gdf3+ sperm display the same embryonic lethal MZgdf3 mutant phenotype as those fertilized with sperm from a homozygous gdf3- mutant father.
evidence: This is based on reciprocal cross experiments.

claim: Zygotic expression of wildtype gdf3 from the paternal genome after zygotic gene activation is insufficient to rescue the MZgdf3 mutant phenotype.
source: This indicates that zygotic expression of wildtype gdf3, confirmed by allele-specific RT-PCR, from the paternal genome after zygotic gene activation (ZGA, 4.2 hpf) (Lee et al., 2014), is insufficient rescue the MZgdf3 mutant phenotype.
evidence: This is based on RT-PCR analysis and phenotypic observations with citation to Lee et al., 2014.

claim: The inability to rescue the MZ phenotype may reflect the timing and/or levels of zygotic expression.
source: The inability to rescue the MZ phenotype may reflect the timing and/or levels of zygotic expression.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The embryonic lethal MZgdf3 phenotype can be rescued to grow to viable fertile adults when injected with gdf3 RNA at the 1 cell to 2 cell stages.
source: The embryonic lethal MZgdf3 phenotype can however, be rescued to grow to viable fertile adults when injected with gdf3 RNA at the 1 cell to 2 cell stages, supporting the idea that Gdf3 is essential during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This is based on rescue experiments.

claim: Gdf3 is essential during early embryogenesis.
source: The embryonic lethal MZgdf3 phenotype can however, be rescued to grow to viable fertile adults when injected with gdf3 RNA at the 1 cell to 2 cell stages, supporting the idea that Gdf3 is essential during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments.

claim: Murine Gdf3 mutants phenocopy early germ layer and axial phenotypes of Nodal mutants.
source: Murine Gdf3 mutants (Chen et al., 2006) phenocopy early germ layer and axial phenotypes of Nodal mutants while Gdf1 mutants (Rankin et al., 2000; Wall et al., 2000) phenocopy the laterality phenotypes of node-specific Nodal mutants.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2006.

claim: Murine Gdf1 mutants phenocopy the laterality phenotypes of node-specific Nodal mutants.
source: Murine Gdf3 mutants (Chen et al., 2006) phenocopy early germ layer and axial phenotypes of Nodal mutants while Gdf1 mutants (Rankin et al., 2000; Wall et al., 2000) phenocopy the laterality phenotypes of node-specific Nodal mutants.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rankin et al., 2000; Wall et al., 2000.

claim: Nodal-Gdf heterodimers are thought to be the functional entity in both germ layer and LR patterning in mice.
source: As we have proposed in this study, and as proposed by Peterson et al. (2013) in zebrafish, Nodal-Gdf heterodimers are thought to be the functional entity in both germ layer and LR patterning in mice (Andersson et al., 2006; Tanaka et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Andersson et al., 2006; Tanaka et al., 2007; Peterson et al., 2013.

claim: The functional ligand for the Nodal signaling pathway during early zebrafish development is an obligate heterodimer of Gdf3/Nodal (Gdf3/Ndr1 and/or Gdf3/Ndr2).
source: Combining our genetic results and these previous biochemical experiments, we suggest that the functional ligand for the Nodal signaling pathway during early zebrafish development is an obligate heterodimer of Gdf3/Nodal (Gdf3/Ndr1 and/or Gdf3/Ndr2), and importantly, that homodimers of either Nodal/Nodal or Gdf3/Gdf3 are not functional in early embryonic patterning.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on genetic and biochemical evidence.

claim: Homodimers of either Nodal/Nodal or Gdf3/Gdf3 are not functional in early embryonic patterning.
source: Combining our genetic results and these previous biochemical experiments, we suggest that the functional ligand for the Nodal signaling pathway during early zebrafish development is an obligate heterodimer of Gdf3/Nodal (Gdf3/Ndr1 and/or Gdf3/Ndr2), and importantly, that homodimers of either Nodal/Nodal or Gdf3/Gdf3 are not functional in early embryonic patterning.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on genetic evidence.

claim: There is precedent for obligate heterodimers from studies of bmp2 and bmp7 during zebrafish dorsoventral patterning, where only the heterodimer possess sufficient receptor activity to elicit the signaling required for DV patterning.
source: There is precedent for this idea from studies of the role of the TGFβ family members bmp2 and bmp7 during zebrafish dorsoventral (DV) patterning. While homodimers of both are found in the embryo, only the heterodimer possess sufficient receptor activity to elicit the signaling required for DV patterning (Little and Mullins, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Little and Mullins, 2009.

claim: There is a single Nodal locus in mammals, whereas there are three Nodal-related loci in zebrafish, ndr1, ndr2 and spaw.
source: There is a single Nodal locus in mammals, whereas there are three Nodal-related loci in zebrafish, ndr1, which is maternally expressed, and ndr2 and spaw which are zygotic (Long et al., 2003; Rebagliati et al., 1998a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Long et al., 2003; Rebagliati et al., 1998a.

claim: ndr1 is maternally expressed, and ndr2 and spaw are zygotic.
source: There is a single Nodal locus in mammals, whereas there are three Nodal-related loci in zebrafish, ndr1, which is maternally expressed, and ndr2 and spaw which are zygotic (Long et al., 2003; Rebagliati et al., 1998a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Long et al., 2003; Rebagliati et al., 1998a.

claim: The early embryonic functions of mouse Nodal, in germ layer and axial development, are reflected by the functions of zebrafish paralogs Ndr1 and Ndr2 during cleavage and gastrulation.
source: The early embryonic functions of mouse Nodal, in germ layer and axial development (Brennan et al., 2001; Conlon et al., 1994; Varlet et al., 1997), are reflected by the functions of zebrafish paralogs Ndr1 and Ndr2 during cleavage and gastrulation (Feldman et al., 1998; Rebagliati et al., 1998a, 1998b; Sampath et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple papers.

claim: The role of murine Nodal in Left-Right patterning appears to be accomplished by Spaw and Ndr2 during somitogenesis in zebrafish.
source: The role of murine Nodal in Left-Right patterning (Brennan et al., 2002; Saijoh et al., 2003) appears to be accomplished by Spaw and Ndr2 during somitogenesis in zebrafish (Long et al., 2003; Rebagliati et al., 1998a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple papers.

claim: There is a single locus of the gdf gene family in zebrafish, gdf3, whereas there are two related loci in mammalian genomes, ancestral Gdf3 and more recently derived Gdf1.
source: In an inversion of the usual comparisons between the mammalian and duplicated zebrafish genomes, there is a single locus of the gdf gene family in zebrafish, gdf3, whereas there are two related loci in mammalian genomes, ancestral Gdf3 and more recently derived Gdf1.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the evolutionary relationships.
